## 5. Regulatory Liquidity Reporting and Basel III Metadata

This sub-topic covers the authoritative terminology and regulatory metrics required for banking compliance and treasury operations.

### Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Rules
*   **LCR Core Definition:** A binding regulatory metric requiring a bank to hold sufficient High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to cover total net cash outflows over a 30-calendar-day stress scenario [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).
*   **Calculation Constraints:**
    $$\text{LCR} = \frac{\text{HQLA}}{\text{Total Net Cash Outflows over 30 Days}}$$
    *   HQLA assets are split into Level 1 and Level 2 tiers, applying mandated regulatory haircuts [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).
    *   Net cash outflows are modeled by applying standardized run-off rates to liabilities and capping inflows on receivables [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).
*   **Floor Limits and Violations:** The regulatory minimum floor for LCR is exactly 100%. Any operating target exceeding this is an internal risk-appetite decision, not a regulatory minimum. A breach of the 100% floor—even intraday on reporting dates—is a mandatory notifiable event requiring immediate escalation to Treasury and Regulatory Reporting leads [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).

## 1. Inventory & Supply Chain Metadata Definitions
This section maps the relationships, definitions, and system identifiers used across planning, procurement, and warehouse operations.

### Core Identifiers & Mapping rules
*   **SKU (Stock Keeping Unit):** The internal identifier for a distinct, sellable product variant (representing a specific size, color, and pack configuration). It is the hub of the planning stack and the unit at which inventory is held, forecasted, and replenished across all distribution centers [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md).
    *   *System Rule:* Do not confuse SKU with UPC/GTIN. A product can have one UPC but several SKUs over its life cycle; treating them as identical causes system double-counting [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md).
*   **UPC / GTIN:** An external, industry-wide barcode standard assigned for retail scanning. It is stored in internal systems purely as an attribute mapped back to an internal SKU [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md).
*   **Bill of Materials (BOM):** The multi-level structured recipe for a finished-good SKU, listing every component, sub-assembly, and corresponding quantities needed to build a single finished unit. It serves as the single source of truth linking finished SKUs to component material procurement [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md), [Procurement Standard Operating Procedure](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/procurement_sop.md).

### Metrics & Replenishment Parameters
*   **Lead Time:** The total elapsed time from when a purchase order (PO) is placed with a supplier until the goods are received, inspected, and posted as available ("good" quantity) to pick. It includes supplier processing, transit, and inbound handling [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Procurement Standard Operating Procedure](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/procurement_sop.md).
    *   *Inbound Lead Time:* Time from supplier PO to receipt at a Regional DC [Logistics Network Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/logistics_network_overview.md).
    *   *Inter-node Lead Time:* Transit time required to move stock from a Regional DC to a Forward DC [Logistics Network Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/logistics_network_overview.md).
*   **Safety Stock (Buffer Stock):** Extra inventory held to protect against demand spikes and lead-time variability. It is sized in days of supply or against target service levels, categorized by SKU velocity class [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
    *   *Class A (Fast Movers):* 14 days of supply [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
    *   *Class B:* 10 days of supply [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
    *   *Class C:* 7 days of supply [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
*   **Reorder Point (ROP):** The ERP-labeled system field indicating the on-hand inventory level that automatically triggers a replenishment order [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
    *   *Formula:* $ROP = (\text{Average Daily Demand} \times \text{Lead Time in Days}) + \text{Safety Stock}$ [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).

## 2. Finance & Customer Analytics Metrics
This section reconciles naming variations and metrics definitions used across financial modeling and marketing dashboards.

*   **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV / LTV):** The total net profit expected from a customer across their entire relationship. It is calculated as projected revenue minus the combined cost to serve and retain them [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md), [Marketing Analytics — Deck Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/marketing_analytics_deck_notes.md).
    *   *Synonym Reconciliation:* Finance dashboards label this metric **CLV**, whereas marketing decks use **customer LTV** or **LTV**. These terms represent the same metric and must not be treated as distinct measures [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md), [Marketing Analytics — Deck Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/marketing_analytics_deck_notes.md).
*   **Net Interest Margin (NIM):** A profitability metric reported in earnings and treasury reviews, calculated as:
    $$\text{Net Interest Margin} = \frac{\text{Net Interest Income}}{\text{Average Interest-Earning Assets}}$$
    It expresses the margin produced per dollar of earning assets and fluctuates with the interest-rate environment [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).
*   **Credit Risk Score:** A quantified estimate of borrower default probability built from repayment history, current exposure, and leverage/income. Used for loan pricing and portfolio monitoring [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).
    *   *Distinction:* Must be kept distinct from the **KYC Risk Rating**, which specifically measures financial-crime risk rather than credit default risk [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).

This section defines metadata and core entities supporting network engineering, provisioning, and regulatory compliance.

*   **IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity):** The globally unique identifier of a subscriber provisioned onto the physical SIM card. It is the primary key reference used by the network for authentication, home connections, and roaming [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md).

# Metadata Enrichment: Knowledge Base Synthesis

This document synthesizes key business concepts, terminologies, and operational procedures across treasury operations, supply chain logistics, and corporate policies to support metadata enrichment and taxonomy development.

## 1. Financial Systems, Treasury, and Regulatory Metrics
Metadata enrichment for financial systems must capture key formulas, balance-sheet metrics, and trade settlement operations to ensure accurate reporting and compliance.

### Balance-Sheet Profitability and Liquidity Metrics
*   **Net Interest Margin (NIM):** The core measure of balance-sheet profitability, representing how efficiently a financial institution converts its balance sheet into net interest income. It is calculated using the following formula: 
    $$\text{NIM} = \frac{\text{Interest Income} - \text{Interest Expense}}{\text{Average Earning Assets}}$$
    NIM must be actively monitored against the rate environment, as rising funding costs that outpace asset yields will compress the margin. Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).
*   **Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR):** An essential liquidity metric defined under Basel III regulations. It measures the ratio of High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to 30-day net cash outflows. While regulatory minimums apply, internal management targets are maintained with headroom at approximately 110%. LCR forecasts are updated daily. Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).

### Trade Settlement Operations
*   **T+1 Settlement:** The finalization of equities and most fixed-income trades through the exchange of cash and securities occurs on a $T+1$ basis (one business day after the trade date). Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).
*   **Settlement Processing Cutoffs:** Daily trade instructions must be submitted before the standing processing cutoff of **16:00 ET** (governed by the Trade Operations Runbook) to settle in that day's batch. Instructions received after this cutoff roll over and settle on the following business day. Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).

---

## 2. Supply Chain, Logistics, and Inventory Management
Taxonomy development for physical operations requires distinct classification of nodes, inventory tracking granularities, and escalation pathways.

### Distribution Center (DC) Node Operations
*   **Network Role:** A distribution center (or "fulfillment center/node") acts as an intermediary node in the logistics network, receiving bulk inventory from upstream suppliers and fulfilling downstream orders for retail stores or end customers. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Inventory Independence:** Each DC holds, tracks, and counts its inventory independently. Consequently, the same Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) can have highly variable on-hand quantities across different DCs, and replenishment decisions are calculated on a per-DC basis. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

### Inventory Tracking and Control
*   **SKU-Level Tracking:** Putaway and cycle counts must be executed and scanned at the precise SKU level rather than the general product family. Failure to do so leads to downstream picking failures. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Inbound Quality Control:** Inbound inventory processes require verifying carton counts against the Purchase Order (PO). Good items are posted as available, whereas damaged units are immediately quarantined. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Reorder Dynamics:** Real-time on-hand SKU positions directly feed the planning system's reorder calculations. Inaccurate cycle counts negatively affect the timing of replenishment triggers. If a DC experiences an out-of-stock event for a SKU, order routers may dynamically source the item from another DC in the network. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

### Operational Escalation Workflows
*   **Receiving Mismatches:** Discrepancies between physical inbound counts and the PO must be escalated to **Procurement**. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Persistent Stockouts:** Continuous stockouts of fast-moving SKUs require escalation to **Demand Planning** to re-evaluate safety stock levels and reorder points. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

## 3. Corporate Compliance and Expense Governance
Standardizing metadata for corporate policies ensures compliance engines can automatically flag exceptions and route approvals.

### Corporate Travel and Expense Rules
*   **Booking Channels:** All travel (flights and hotels) must be booked through the approved corporate travel tool. Out-of-tool bookings are non-reimbursable without prior manager approval. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Flight Class Policies:** Economy class is standard for flights under six hours. Premium economy is permitted for longer flights only with director-level sign-off. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Lodging and Meals:** Hotel selections must conform to published per-city nightly caps, and daily meals must align with published per-diem rates by city. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Ground Transportation:** Standard ride-share or taxi services are reimbursable; luxury tiers of ride-share or taxi services are strictly prohibited. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).

### Financial Control and Auditing
*   **Submission Timelines:** Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of the spend date. Submissions older than 60 days are flagged and require an exception approval. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Receipt Thresholds:** Itemized receipts are mandatory for any expense exceeding the established corporate receipt threshold. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Corporate Card Governance:** Mixing personal expenses on corporate cards is prohibited. If accidental mixing occurs, personal transactions must be flagged immediately and reimbursed to the company. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Approval Routing:**

# Metadata Compliance Auditor Overview

The Metadata Compliance Auditor is an automated auditing tool designed to continuously scan metadata repositories. It audits corporate data and transactional metadata against compliance policies, financial controls, and corporate expense guidelines. Its primary function is to ensure that these repositories comply with both enterprise-specific standards and regulatory requirements.

## Category
This entry belongs to the `Financial and Regulatory Metadata` category.

## Key Responsibilities

The Metadata Compliance Auditor plays a critical role in ensuring data integrity and adherence to organizational policies and regulatory mandates by auditing various metadata points. Its responsibilities include:

*   **Corporate Expense Governance**: It verifies adherence to corporate travel and expense policies outlined in the `Corporate Travel & Expense Policy`. This includes auditing metadata related to:
    *   **Booking Channels**: Ensuring all travel (flights and hotels) is booked through approved corporate tools, flagging out-of-tool bookings for prior manager approval.
    *   **Flight Class Policies**: Verifying adherence to flight class standards, such as economy for flights under six hours, and requiring director-level sign-off for premium economy on longer flights.
    *   **Lodging and Meals**: Checking compliance with published per-city nightly caps for hotels and per-diem rates for meals.
    *   **Ground Transportation**: Confirming the use of standard ride-share or taxi services and strictly prohibiting luxury tiers.
*   **Financial Controls**: The Auditor examines financial control metadata, such as:
    *   **Expense Submission Timelines**: Ensuring expenses are submitted within 30 days of the spend date, and flagging submissions older than 60 days for exception approval.
    *   **Receipt Thresholds**: Verifying that itemized receipts are provided for expenses exceeding established corporate thresholds.
    *   **Corporate Card Governance**: Auditing against the mixing of personal expenses on corporate cards, requiring immediate flagging and reimbursement if accidental mixing occurs.
    *   **Approval Routing**: Ensuring correct routing of standard expense reports to direct managers and policy exceptions to both the direct manager and Finance Shared Services for secondary auditing.
*   **Regulatory Compliance**: The Auditor supports adherence to broader regulatory and financial metadata policies by cross-referencing information against defined standards, including:
    *   **KYC Profile Creation**: Verifying the completion of Know Your Customer (KYC) / Customer Due Diligence (CDD) verification for new customer accounts before activation, as per the `Customer Onboarding SOP`.
    *   **Risk Ratings**: Distinguishing between and ensuring correct application of KYC Risk Ratings (for financial-crime risk) and Credit Risk Scores (for borrower default probability) where applicable, as noted in the `Compliance Policy Handbook` and `Finance Business Glossary`.
    *   **Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)**: Potentially verifying metadata related to the calculation and adherence to the regulatory minimums for LCR, as defined under Basel III regulations in the `Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary`.

# Liquidity Coverage Ratio Rules Overview

The Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) is a critical regulatory and treasury metric defined under Basel III regulations, designed to ensure that banks maintain sufficient high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) to cover potential net cash outflows during a 30-calendar-day stress scenario. As a fundamental piece of financial and risk metadata, LCR serves as a key indicator of an institution's short-term liquidity resilience.

## Definition and Calculation

The LCR is calculated as the ratio of High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to total net cash outflows over a 30-day period:

$$\text{LCR} = \frac{\text{HQLA}}{\text{Total Net Cash Outflows over 30 Days}}$$

*   **High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA):** These assets are categorized into Level 1 and Level 2 tiers, and mandated regulatory haircuts are applied to their values.
*   **Total Net Cash Outflows:** These are modeled by applying standardized run-off rates to liabilities and by capping inflows on receivables.

LCR forecasts are updated daily to reflect current conditions and projections.

## Regulatory Compliance and Monitoring

The regulatory minimum floor for LCR is **100%**. While internal management targets may exceed this (e.g., maintaining headroom at approximately 110% as an internal risk-appetite decision), any breach of the 100% floor, even intraday on reporting dates, constitutes a mandatory notifiable event. Such a breach requires immediate escalation to Treasury and Regulatory Reporting leads. The LCR is explicitly identified as a "regulatory liquidity metric" within the broader category of "Financial & Risk Metadata," highlighting its importance for compliance and risk management.

# Master Scope: Metadata Enrichment

The following structured findings synthesize metadata-enrichment concepts, cross-domain terminologies, and operational relationships extracted from the source corpus.

---

## 1. Customer Profiles and Financial-Crime Risk Metadata

This sub-topic details how customer metadata is captured at onboarding, how risk ratings are defined, and how these data points are leveraged downstream during transaction monitoring and anti-money laundering (AML) investigations.

### Onboarding Metadata and Risk Categorization
*   **KYC Profile Creation:** Every new customer account requires completing Know Your Customer (KYC) / Customer Due Diligence (CDD) verification. Activating an account prior to KYC verification is a critical process error. Non-individual customer onboarding requires establishing beneficial ownership [Customer Onboarding SOP](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_onboarding_sop.md).
*   **Risk Ratings vs. Credit Scores:** It is a critical error to confuse financial-crime risk metadata with credit-risk metadata. They serve distinct purposes and are defined as follows:
    *   **KYC Risk Rating:** Categorizes customers into standard or enhanced due diligence (EDD) bands to assess financial-crime risk [Compliance Policy Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/compliance_policy_handbook.md), [Customer Onboarding SOP](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_onboarding_sop.md).
    *   **Credit Risk Score:** Quantifies the likelihood of borrower default based on repayment history, existing exposure, income, and leverage to determine pricing limits and credit terms [Customer Onboarding SOP](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_onboarding_sop.md).
*   **Downstream Persistence:** Both the KYC risk rating and credit risk score are persisted as structural metadata on the customer profile to guide downstream monitoring, servicing, and manual underwriting [Customer Onboarding SOP](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_onboarding_sop.md).

### Transaction Monitoring & AML Alert Investigations
*   **Risk-Based Monitoring:** Ongoing transaction monitoring is risk-based, leveraging the customer's KYC profile and assigned risk rating to detect deviations from expected behaviors (e.g., unusual volumes, structuring patterns, or inconsistent fund movements) [AML Investigations Playbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/aml_investigations_playbook.md), [Compliance Policy Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/compliance_policy_handbook.md).
*   **Investigation Workflow Metadata:**
    *   **Step 1 (Context Review):** Investigators pull the KYC file to evaluate the customer's identity, expected activity, and risk rating. Stale KYC metadata must trigger a profile refresh [AML Investigations Playbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/aml_investigations_playbook.md).
    *   **Step 2 (Reconstruct Activity):** Flows of funds are actively traced and compared directly against expected profile parameters [AML Investigations Playbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/aml_investigations_playbook.md).
    *   **Step 3 (Disposition & Escalation):** Findings of reasonable suspicion must be formally documented to connect the observed activity to the suspicion (the subjective metadata "looked odd" is insufficient) and escalated to a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) [AML Investigations Playbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/aml_investigations_playbook.md), [Compliance Policy Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/compliance_policy_handbook.md).
*   **Regulatory SAR Metadata Constraints:**
    *   **Confidentiality (No Tipping Off):** Under no circumstances may customer-facing metadata or accounts indicate that a SAR is contemplated or has been filed [AML Investigations Playbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/aml_investigations_playbook.md), [Compliance Policy Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/compliance_policy_handbook.md).
    *   **Time-Bounded Window:** A regulatory filing window begins immediately when suspicion is established [AML Investigations Playbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/aml_investigations_playbook.md), [Compliance Policy Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/compliance_policy_handbook.md).

---

## 2. Subscriber Lifecycle, Billing, and Commercial Telecommunications Metadata

This sub-topic details how telecommunications metadata links customer care operations, commercial lifecycle statuses, billing system logic, and subscriber churn risk profiles.

### Billing and Charge Rating Systems
*   **Rating vs. Billing Phases:** Billing systems process raw usage events into invoices in two stages:
    *   **Rating:** Applies the subscriber's price plan metadata to raw usage events to calculate individual charges [Billing & Charging System Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/billing_charging_system_overview.md).
    *   **Billing:** Aggregates rated charges over a recurring, customer-specific billing cycle [Billing & Charging System Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/billing_charging_system_overview.md).
*   **Cycle Staggering & Staggering Logic:** System cycle boundaries are staggered across the customer base to distribute invoicing and system processing loads throughout the month rather than spiking on a single day [Billing & Charging System Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/billing_charging_system_overview.md).
*   **Plan-Type Attributes:**
    *   **Postpaid:** Usage is rated, accumulated, reconciled, and invoiced in arrears at the close of the billing cycle [Billing & Charging System Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/billing_charging_system_overview.md), [Customer Care Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_care_handbook.md).
    *   **Prepaid:** Usage charges are decremented in real time against a monetary balance, making the "billing cycle" metadata a window for plan allowances rather than invoice generation [Billing & Charging System Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/billing_charging_system_overview.md).

### Number Portability Metadata
*   **System Identifiers:** Number portability allows subscribers to retain their phone numbers when changing carriers. It is represented interchangeably in systems by the metadata labels "Porting," "LNP" (Local Number Portability), or "MNP" (Mobile Number Portability) [Customer Care Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_care_handbook.md).
*   **Porting State Tracking:** To initiate a transfer, agents collect account details to open a port request. This triggers a "validation window" status during which the losing carrier verifies details. Porting delays past this window are escalated to the Provisioning team [Customer Care Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_care_handbook.md).

### Churn and Customer Attrition Analytics
*   **Analytical Equivalence:** Customer churn and customer attrition are identical commercial measures, defined as the percentage of the subscriber base that deactivates during a specific quarter [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md), [Customer Care Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_care_handbook.md).
*   **Churn Driver Segmentation:** Voluntary churn is driven primarily by Price, Network Quality, and Competitor Offers [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).
*   **Risk Profiles & Stickiness Attributes:**
    *   **Contract Status:** Price-driven churn is heavily concentrated among out-of-contract subscribers [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).
    *   **Product Depth:** Single-product subscribers are far more susceptible to churn than multi-service subscribers, demonstrating that deeper relationship profiles are stickier [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).
    *   **Targeting Logic:** Analytics recommends mapping subscriber profiles against Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) to direct retention and incentive budgets to high-value, at-risk subscriber segments [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).

---

## 3. Network Quality of Service (QoS) and Charging System Integration

This sub-topic details how network-level quality of service (QoS) parameters, real-time data throttling, and Voice-over-LTE (VoLTE) performance targets are defined and shared across systems.

### Policy Function & Data Throttling Integration
*   **Dynamic Policy Signaling:** Charging systems dynamically coordinate with the network policy function. When a data plan threshold is crossed, the charging system signals the policy function to assign a lower-priority QoS class (commonly referred to as "throttling") for the remainder of the billing cycle [Billing & Charging System Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/billing_charging_system_overview.md).

### Voice over LTE (VoLTE) Latency Specifications
*   **QoS Class Dependency:** VoLTE voice traffic is treated as packets requiring the "conversational-voice" QoS class [Postmortem: Metro Region Dropped-Calls Incident](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/dropped_calls_postmortem.md).
*   **Threshold Alignment:** Real-world testing revealed that legacy QoS Policy metadata (which tolerated a one-way packet latency budget of 100 ms) did not align with modern VoLTE codecs and jitter profiles, resulting in audible clipping and dropped calls before alarms fired. Latency targets for the conversational-voice class must be tightened to 80 ms to ensure acceptable service quality [Postmortem: Metro Region Dropped-Calls Incident](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/dropped_calls_postmortem.md).

---

## 4. Operational Assets, Supply Chain, and Inventory Metadata

This sub-topic details the metadata structures utilized in engineering designs, manufacturing procurement, and retail inventory management.

### Bill of Materials (BOM) Specifications
*   **BOM Hierarchy:** The Bill of Materials (BOM) is a multi-level tree structure representing the authoritative definition of finished goods, sub-assemblies, and components required to build a product [Bill of Materials — Engineering Specification](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/bom_spec.md).
*   **Reusability & Versioning:** A sub-assembly's BOM is defined once and referenced globally. Revisions are strictly versioned so production operates on a known recipe. Only engineering may modify these specifications [Bill of Materials — Engineering Specification](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/bom_spec.md).
*   **MRP Explosion:** When a demand forecast is entered at the finished-good SKU level, the planning system automatically "explodes" the requirements by multiplying parent demand by the per-unit quantities at every sub-assembly and component level to generate procurement purchase demands [Bill of Materials — Engineering Specification](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/bom_spec.md).

### Inventory Policy Control Parameters
*   **Safety Stock:** The inventory cushion held above the demand forecast to absorb variability in demand or late inbound shipments [Demand Planning — Weekly Sync Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/demand_planning_meeting_notes.md).
*   **Reorder Point:** The inventory trigger that initiates replenishment. Rather than modifying the reorder point directly, planners recalculate the safety stock based on current demand variability, allowing the reorder point (calculated as safety stock plus demand-over-lead-time) to adjust automatically [Demand Planning — Weekly Sync Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/demand_planning_meeting_notes.md).

## 5. Regulatory Liquidity Reporting and Basel III Metadata

This sub-topic covers the authoritative terminology and regulatory metrics required for banking compliance and treasury operations.

### Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Rules
*   **LCR Core Definition:** A binding regulatory metric requiring a bank to hold sufficient High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to cover total net cash outflows over a 30-calendar-day stress scenario [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).
*   **Calculation Constraints:**
    $$\text{LCR} = \frac{\text{HQLA}}{\text{Total Net Cash Outflows over 30 Days}}$$
    *   HQLA assets are split into Level 1 and Level 2 tiers, applying mandated regulatory haircuts [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).
    *   Net cash outflows are modeled by applying standardized run-off rates to liabilities and capping inflows on receivables [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).
*   **Floor Limits and Violations:** The regulatory minimum floor for LCR is exactly 100%. Any operating target exceeding this is an internal risk-appetite decision, not a regulatory minimum. A breach of the 100% floor—even intraday on reporting dates—is a mandatory notifiable event requiring immediate escalation to Treasury and Regulatory Reporting leads [Basel III Regulatory Filing — Internal Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/basel_iii_filing_summary.md).

# Metadata Enrichment: Knowledge Base Synthesis

This document synthesizes metadata, operational definitions, and relational concepts extracted from the corpus. To support metadata enrichment and schema development, findings are organized by logical domain under the unified project scope.

---

## 1. Inventory & Supply Chain Metadata Definitions
This section maps the relationships, definitions, and system identifiers used across planning, procurement, and warehouse operations.

### Core Identifiers & Mapping rules
*   **SKU (Stock Keeping Unit):** The internal identifier for a distinct, sellable product variant (representing a specific size, color, and pack configuration). It is the hub of the planning stack and the unit at which inventory is held, forecasted, and replenished across all distribution centers [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md).
    *   *System Rule:* Do not confuse SKU with UPC/GTIN. A product can have one UPC but several SKUs over its life cycle; treating them as identical causes system double-counting [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md).
*   **UPC / GTIN:** An external, industry-wide barcode standard assigned for retail scanning. It is stored in internal systems purely as an attribute mapped back to an internal SKU [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md).
*   **Bill of Materials (BOM):** The multi-level structured recipe for a finished-good SKU, listing every component, sub-assembly, and corresponding quantities needed to build a single finished unit. It serves as the single source of truth linking finished SKUs to component material procurement [Inventory Systems Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_systems_overview.md), [Procurement Standard Operating Procedure](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/procurement_sop.md).

### Metrics & Replenishment Parameters
*   **Lead Time:** The total elapsed time from when a purchase order (PO) is placed with a supplier until the goods are received, inspected, and posted as available ("good" quantity) to pick. It includes supplier processing, transit, and inbound handling [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Procurement Standard Operating Procedure](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/procurement_sop.md).
    *   *Inbound Lead Time:* Time from supplier PO to receipt at a Regional DC [Logistics Network Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/logistics_network_overview.md).
    *   *Inter-node Lead Time:* Transit time required to move stock from a Regional DC to a Forward DC [Logistics Network Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/logistics_network_overview.md).
*   **Safety Stock (Buffer Stock):** Extra inventory held to protect against demand spikes and lead-time variability. It is sized in days of supply or against target service levels, categorized by SKU velocity class [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
    *   *Class A (Fast Movers):* 14 days of supply [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
    *   *Class B:* 10 days of supply [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
    *   *Class C:* 7 days of supply [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).
*   **Reorder Point (ROP):** The ERP-labeled system field indicating the on-hand inventory level that automatically triggers a replenishment order [Inventory Management Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_management_glossary.md), [Inventory Policy Memo](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/inventory_policy_memo.md).

## 2. Finance & Customer Analytics Metrics
This section reconciles naming variations and metrics definitions used across financial modeling and marketing dashboards.

*   **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV / LTV):** The total net profit expected from a customer across their entire relationship. It is calculated as projected revenue minus the combined cost to serve and retain them [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md), [Marketing Analytics — Deck Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/marketing_analytics_deck_notes.md).
    *   *Synonym Reconciliation:* Finance dashboards label this metric **CLV**, whereas marketing decks use **customer LTV** or **LTV**. These terms represent the same metric and must not be treated as distinct measures [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md), [Marketing Analytics — Deck Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/marketing_analytics_deck_notes.md).
*   **Net Interest Margin (NIM):** A profitability metric reported in earnings and treasury reviews, calculated as:
    $$\text{Net Interest Margin} = \frac{\text{Net Interest Income}}{\text{Average Interest-Earning Assets}}$$
    It expresses the margin produced per dollar of earning assets and fluctuates with the interest-rate environment [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).
*   **Credit Risk Score:** A quantified estimate of borrower default probability built from repayment history, current exposure, and leverage/income. Used for loan pricing and portfolio monitoring [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).
    *   *Distinction:* Must be kept distinct from the **KYC Risk Rating**, which specifically measures financial-crime risk rather than credit default risk [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).

This section defines metadata and core entities supporting network engineering, provisioning, and regulatory compliance.

*   **IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity):** The globally unique identifier of a subscriber provisioned onto the physical SIM card. It is the primary key reference used by the network for authentication, home connections, and roaming [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md).
    *   *Synonym Reconciliation:* Avoid the loose term "SIM identity" in engineering documentation; prefer **IMSI** [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md).

Highly dependent on QoS class parameters [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md).
    *   *Synonym Reconciliation:* **Voice-over-LTE**, **VoLTE**, and **IMS Voice** are synonyms representing the exact same service [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md).

# Metadata Enrichment: Knowledge Base Synthesis

This document synthesizes key business concepts, terminologies, and operational procedures across treasury operations, supply chain logistics, and corporate policies to support metadata enrichment and taxonomy development.

---

## 1. Financial Systems, Treasury, and Regulatory Metrics
Metadata enrichment for financial systems must capture key formulas, balance-sheet metrics, and trade settlement operations to ensure accurate reporting and compliance.

### Balance-Sheet Profitability and Liquidity Metrics
*   **Net Interest Margin (NIM):** The core measure of balance-sheet profitability, representing how efficiently a financial institution converts its balance sheet into net interest income. It is calculated using the following formula: 
    $$\text{NIM} = \frac{\text{Interest Income} - \text{Interest Expense}}{\text{Average Earning Assets}}$$
    NIM must be actively monitored against the rate environment, as rising funding costs that outpace asset yields will compress the margin. Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).
*   **Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR):** An essential liquidity metric defined under Basel III regulations. It measures the ratio of High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to 30-day net cash outflows. While regulatory minimums apply, internal management targets are maintained with headroom at approximately 110%. LCR forecasts are updated daily. Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).

### Trade Settlement Operations
*   **T+1 Settlement:** The finalization of equities and most fixed-income trades through the exchange of cash and securities occurs on a $T+1$ basis (one business day after the trade date). Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).
*   **Settlement Processing Cutoffs:** Daily trade instructions must be submitted before the standing processing cutoff of **16:00 ET** (governed by the Trade Operations Runbook) to settle in that day's batch. Instructions received after this cutoff roll over and settle on the following business day. Source: [Treasury Operations Guide](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/treasury_operations_guide.md).

---

## 2. Supply Chain, Logistics, and Inventory Management
Taxonomy development for physical operations requires distinct classification of nodes, inventory tracking granularities, and escalation pathways.

### Distribution Center (DC) Node Operations
*   **Network Role:** A distribution center (or "fulfillment center/node") acts as an intermediary node in the logistics network, receiving bulk inventory from upstream suppliers and fulfilling downstream orders for retail stores or end customers. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Inventory Independence:** Each DC holds, tracks, and counts its inventory independently. Consequently, the same Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) can have highly variable on-hand quantities across different DCs, and replenishment decisions are calculated on a per-DC basis. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

### Inventory Tracking and Control
*   **SKU-Level Tracking:** Putaway and cycle counts must be executed and scanned at the precise SKU level rather than the general product family. Failure to do so leads to downstream picking failures. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Inbound Quality Control:** Inbound inventory processes require verifying carton counts against the Purchase Order (PO). Good items are posted as available, whereas damaged units are immediately quarantined. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Reorder Dynamics:** Real-time on-hand SKU positions directly feed the planning system's reorder calculations. Inaccurate cycle counts negatively affect the timing of replenishment triggers. If a DC experiences an out-of-stock event for a SKU, order routers may dynamically source the item from another DC in the network. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

### Operational Escalation Workflows
*   **Receiving Mismatches:** Discrepancies between physical inbound counts and the PO must be escalated to **Procurement**. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Persistent Stockouts:** Continuous stockouts of fast-moving SKUs require escalation to **Demand Planning** to re-evaluate safety stock levels and reorder points. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

---

## 3. Corporate Compliance and Expense Governance
Standardizing metadata for corporate policies ensures compliance engines can automatically flag exceptions and route approvals.

### Corporate Travel and Expense Rules
*   **Booking Channels:** All travel (flights and hotels) must be booked through the approved corporate travel tool. Out-of-tool bookings are non-reimbursable without prior manager approval. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Flight Class Policies:** Economy class is standard for flights under six hours. Premium economy is permitted for longer flights only with director-level sign-off. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Lodging and Meals:** Hotel selections must conform to published per-city nightly caps, and daily meals must align with published per-diem rates by city. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Ground Transportation:** Standard ride-share or taxi services are reimbursable; luxury tiers of ride-share or taxi services are strictly prohibited. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).

### Financial Control and Auditing
*   **Submission Timelines:** Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of the spend date. Submissions older than 60 days are flagged and require an exception approval. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Receipt Thresholds:** Itemized receipts are mandatory for any expense exceeding the established corporate receipt threshold. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Corporate Card Governance:** Mixing personal expenses on corporate cards is prohibited. If accidental mixing occurs, personal transactions must be flagged immediately and reimbursed to the company. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).
*   **Approval Routing:** 
    *   *Standard Reports:* Route automatically to the claimant's direct manager.
    *   *Policy Exceptions:* Route to both the direct manager and **Finance Shared Services** for secondary auditing.
    *   *Policy Inquiries:* General eligibility questions are handled by the Finance Shared Services help desk. Source: [Corporate Travel & Expense Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/travel_expense_policy.md).

# Credit Risk and KYC Metadata Overview

Credit Risk and KYC Metadata define distinct customer risk profiles, differentiating default probabilities from financial-crime and money laundering risk ratings. These profiles serve as critical structural metadata on customer records, enabling robust metadata enrichment for various downstream financial processes and regulatory compliance.

## Key Concepts and Definitions

This entry encompasses two primary, distinct metadata types:

*   **KYC Risk Rating**: This metadata categorizes customers into bands, such as standard or enhanced due diligence (EDD), to assess their financial-crime risk. This categorization is established during **KYC Profile Creation**, a mandatory step for every new customer account, where Know Your Customer (KYC) / Customer Due Diligence (CDD) verification is completed. Activating an account without prior KYC verification is considered a critical process error. For non-individual customers, establishing beneficial ownership is also required.
*   **Credit Risk Score**: This metadata quantifies the likelihood of a borrower defaulting on their obligations. It is derived from factors such as repayment history, existing exposure, income, and leverage. The Credit Risk Score is used to determine pricing limits and credit terms.

It is a critical distinction that financial-crime risk metadata (KYC Risk Rating) and credit-risk metadata (Credit Risk Score) serve distinct purposes and must not be confused. The KYC Risk Rating specifically measures financial-crime risk, while the Credit Risk Score measures credit default risk.

## Metadata Enrichment and Persistence

Both the KYC Risk Rating and Credit Risk Score are persisted as structural metadata on the customer's profile. This persistence is crucial for guiding subsequent operations and ensuring the accuracy and context of financial data.

## Downstream Application

These metadata elements are leveraged across various operational and analytical functions:

*   **Monitoring and Underwriting**: They guide downstream monitoring, servicing, and manual underwriting processes.
*   **Transaction Monitoring**: Ongoing transaction monitoring is risk-based, utilizing the customer's KYC profile and assigned risk rating to detect deviations from expected behaviors, such as unusual volumes, structuring patterns, or inconsistent fund movements.
*   **AML Alert Investigations**: During anti-money laundering (AML) investigations, investigators pull the KYC file to evaluate the customer's identity, expected activity, and risk rating. Stale KYC metadata in these processes automatically triggers a profile refresh to ensure accuracy.
*   **Risk Management and Provisioning**: Individual Credit Risk Scores are aggregated to feed expected-loss provisioning models and serve as key portfolio health metrics for overall risk management.

## Regulatory and Operational Constraints

Metadata related to financial crime investigations is subject to strict regulatory constraints:

*   **Confidentiality (No Tipping Off)**: Customer-facing metadata or accounts must under no circumstances indicate that a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) is contemplated or has been filed.
*   **Time-Bounded Window**: The regulatory filing window for a SAR begins immediately once suspicion is established.

*   [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md)
*   [AML Investigations Playbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/aml_investigations_playbook.md)
*   [Risk Management Framework](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/risk_management_framework.md)

# Net Interest Margin Metric Overview

The Net Interest Margin (NIM), also known as nim, is a core profitability metric that measures the net interest income generated per dollar of interest-earning assets. It represents how efficiently a financial institution converts its balance sheet into net interest income and is reported in earnings and treasury reviews.

## Definition and Calculation

NIM is a key measure of balance-sheet profitability. It expresses the margin produced per dollar of earning assets and fluctuates with the interest-rate environment.

The Net Interest Margin is calculated using the following formula:

$$\text{NIM} = \frac{\text{Interest Income} - \text{Interest Expense}}{\text{Average Earning Assets}}$$

NIM must be actively monitored against the rate environment, as rising funding costs that outpace asset yields can compress the margin.

# International Mobile Subscriber Identity Overview

The International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) is a globally unique identifier for a mobile subscriber, provisioned onto the physical SIM card. It serves as the primary key for authentication and network attachments, essential for mobile telecommunications systems.

## Key Features and Role

*   **Globally Unique Identifier**: The IMSI is the unique identifier of a subscriber, stored directly on the SIM card.
*   **Primary Key for Network Interaction**: It functions as the primary key reference for networks to authenticate subscribers, manage home connections, and handle roaming.
*   **Roaming and Billing**: IMSI ranges are used in roaming and billing processes to distinguish between a network's home subscribers and visiting subscribers on partner networks.
*   **Network Attachment**: When an IMSI is unregistered, it can lead to network attachment failures, which is a common fault metadata point.
*   **Terminology**: In engineering documentation, it is recommended to prefer the term "IMSI" over the more general "SIM identity."

## Metadata Enrichment and Use Cases

For metadata enrichment, the IMSI is crucial as it represents the fundamental identifier for "which subscriber." In subscriber records, network signaling, and session logs, the IMSI must be treated as the foundational join key for accurate data correlation and analysis.

# Access Point Name Metadata Overview

Access Point Name (APN) Metadata refers to the logical packet network identifier that a mobile device presents to a network. It specifies which packet data network (PDN) and gateway a data session should be routed through, determining the service gateway and dynamic routing policies applied to that session.

## Key Features

An APN is crucial for establishing data connections, as it names the specific packet data network a session connects to, thereby selecting the appropriate gateway and policies for that session. Examples include a public-internet APN or an internal IMS APN used for voice signaling (e.g., for VoLTE).

## Metadata Enrichment Use Cases

For metadata enrichment, APNs serve as a critical identifier in session logs, representing "which service/network" a session accessed. This allows for distinguishing between different types of sessions, such as a general internet APN from an IMS APN used for VoLTE signaling. In common fault metadata, "Attached but no data" alerts often indicate missing or misconfigured APN data profiles, in contrast to network attachment failures which typically map to unregistered IMSIs.

## Aliases

*   APN

# Voice over LTE QoS Overview

Voice over LTE QoS refers to the network policies and packet quality constraints specifically applied to voice sessions carried directly over long-term evolution (LTE) data networks. This topic details how network-level quality of service (QoS) parameters, real-time data throttling, and Voice-over-LTE (VoLTE) performance targets are defined and shared across systems [This sub-topic details how network-level quality of service (QoS) parameters...](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/dropped_calls_postmortem.md). It is also known by the aliases VoLTE and Voice-over-LTE, and internally as IMS Voice [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md).

## Voice over LTE (VoLTE) Definition

VoLTE is a service that carries voice calls as packets over the LTE data network via the IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS), thereby replacing traditional circuit-switched voice paths. The performance and reliability of VoLTE are highly dependent on the QoS class parameters applied to its traffic [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.html).

## Quality of Service (QoS) Parameters for VoLTE

VoLTE voice traffic must be strictly mapped to the "conversational-voice" QoS class [Postmortem: Metro Region Dropped-Calls Incident](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/dropped_calls_postmortem.md), [Quality of Service (QoS) Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/qos_policy_doc.md). Key performance targets for this class include:

*   **One-way packet latency budget**: The target for one-way packet latency must be set to $\le 80\text{ ms}$ to ensure acceptable service quality [Postmortem: Metro Region Dropped-Calls Incident](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/dropped_calls_postmortem.md). Previously, legacy QoS policy metadata tolerated 100 ms, which was found to cause audible clipping and dropped calls with modern VoLTE codecs and jitter profiles [Postmortem: Metro Region Dropped-Calls Incident](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/dropped_calls_postmortem.md).
*   **Packet loss**: Must be less than 1% [Quality of Service (QoS) Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/qos_policy_doc.md).
*   **Guaranteed bit rate**: An end-to-end guaranteed bit rate, appropriate to the voice codec in use, must be enforced to prevent clipping and dropped calls [Quality of Service (QoS) Policy](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/qos_policy_doc.md).

## Associated Subscriber & Session Metadata

For effective metadata enrichment related to VoLTE QoS, several key identifiers are crucial:

*   **IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity)**: This is the globally unique identifier of a subscriber, provisioned onto the physical SIM card. It serves as the primary key reference for network authentication, home connections, and roaming [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md), [Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/telecom_systems_terminology_overview.md). In subscriber records, network signaling, and session logs, the IMSI is the foundational join key representing "which subscriber" [Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/telecom_systems_terminology_overview.md], [SIM Provisioning Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/sim_provisioning_runbook.md). Inter-operator routing, roaming, and billing processes utilize IMSI ranges to distinguish home subscribers from visiting subscribers on partner networks [Roaming Partner Agreement — Summary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/roaming_partner_agreement_summary.md). The term "SIM identity" should be avoided in favor of IMSI [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md).
*   **APN (Access Point Name)**: The APN is an identifier that a mobile device presents to the network to specify which packet data network (e.g., public internet APN or internal IMS APN for voice signaling) and gateway to route a data session through [Network Engineering Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/network_engineering_glossary.md). In session logs, APNs indicate "which service/network" a session accessed, for example, distinguishing a general internet APN from an IMS APN used for VoLTE signaling [Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/telecom_systems_terminology_overview.md). Missing or misconfigured APN data profiles are a common cause for "attached but no data" alerts [SIM Provisioning Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/sim_provisioning_runbook.md).

### Churn and Customer Attrition Analytics
*   **Analytical Equivalence:** Customer churn and customer attrition are identical commercial measures, defined as the percentage of the subscriber base that deactivates during a specific quarter [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md), [Customer Care Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_care_handbook.md).
*   **Churn Driver Segmentation:** Voluntary churn is driven primarily by Price, Network Quality, and Competitor Offers [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).
*   **Risk Profiles & Stickiness Attributes:**
    *   **Contract Status:** Price-driven churn is heavily concentrated among out-of-contract subscribers [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).
    *   **Product Depth:** Single-product subscribers are far more susceptible to churn than multi-service subscribers, demonstrating that deeper relationship profiles are stickier [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).
    *   **Targeting Logic:** Analytics recommends mapping subscriber profiles against Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) to direct retention and incentive budgets to high-value, at-risk subscriber segments [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).

*   **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV / LTV):** The total net profit expected from a customer across their entire relationship. It is calculated as projected revenue minus the combined cost to serve and retain them [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md), [Marketing Analytics — Deck Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/marketing_analytics_deck_notes.md).
    *   *Synonym Reconciliation:* Finance dashboards label this metric **CLV**, whereas marketing decks use **customer LTV** or **LTV**. These terms represent the same metric and must not be treated as distinct measures [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md), [Marketing Analytics — Deck Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/marketing_analytics_deck_notes.md).
*   **Net Interest Margin (NIM):** A profitability metric reported in earnings and treasury reviews, calculated as:
    $$\text{Net Interest Margin} = \frac{\text{Net Interest Income}}{\text{Average Interest-Earning Assets}}$$
    It expresses the margin produced per dollar of earning assets and fluctuates with the interest-rate environment [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).
*   **Credit Risk Score:** A quantified estimate of borrower default probability built from repayment history, current exposure, and leverage/income. Used for loan pricing and portfolio monitoring [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).
    *   *Distinction:* Must be kept distinct from the **KYC Risk Rating**, which specifically measures financial-crime risk rather than credit default risk [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md).

# Subscriber Churn and Lifecycle Analytics Overview

This entry provides metadata for understanding and managing subscriber attrition, contract status, and customer lifetime value within the telecommunications sector. It connects customer care operations, commercial lifecycle statuses, billing system logic, and subscriber churn risk profiles.

## Key Concepts and Definitions

*   **Customer Churn / Attrition**: These terms are analytically equivalent and refer to the percentage of the subscriber base that deactivates during a specific quarter.
    *   Voluntary churn is primarily driven by factors such as Price, Network Quality, and Competitor Offers.
    *   Churn analysis is detailed in the [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md) and related to the [Customer Care Handbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/customer_care_handbook.md).

*   **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV / LTV)**: This metric represents the total net profit expected from a customer throughout their entire relationship with the company. It is calculated as projected revenue minus the combined cost to serve and retain them.
    *   Finance dashboards typically label this metric as **CLV**, while marketing decks use **customer LTV** or simply **LTV**. These terms denote the same metric and should not be treated as distinct measures, as noted in the [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md) and [Marketing Analytics — Deck Notes](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/marketing_analytics_deck_notes.md).

## Subscriber Metadata for Churn Risk and Retention

This topic emphasizes how specific subscriber attributes serve as critical metadata for assessing churn risk and informing retention strategies:

*   **Contract Status**: Subscribers who are out-of-contract are significantly more prone to price-driven churn. This status is a key metadata point for identifying vulnerable segments.
*   **Product Depth**: Single-product subscribers exhibit higher churn susceptibility compared to multi-service subscribers, indicating that deeper product relationships result in greater customer stickiness. The number of products a subscriber uses is therefore important enrichment metadata.
*   **Targeting Logic**: To effectively direct retention and incentive budgets, subscriber profiles are mapped against their Customer Lifetime Value (CLV). This allows for targeting high-value, at-risk subscriber segments.

These metadata attributes and their relationship to churn are discussed in the [Churn Analysis — Quarterly Report](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/churn_analysis_quarterly_report.md).

## Related Financial Metrics

The [Finance Business Glossary](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval%20corpus/finance_business_glossary.md) also references other financial metrics, distinct from subscriber churn and CLV but relevant for broader financial analysis:

*   **Net Interest Margin (NIM)**: A profitability metric reported in earnings and treasury reviews, calculated as:
    $$\text{Net Interest Margin} = \frac{\text{Net Interest Income}}{\text{Average Interest-Earning Assets}}$$
    NIM expresses the margin produced per dollar of earning assets and fluctuates with the interest-rate environment.
*   **Credit Risk Score**: A quantified estimate of a borrower's probability of default, derived from repayment history, current exposure, and leverage/income. It is used for loan pricing and portfolio monitoring.
    *   This score must be distinguished from the **KYC Risk Rating**, which specifically assesses financial-crime risk rather than credit default risk.

# Bill of Materials Specification Overview

The Bill of Materials (BOM), also known as a BOM Specification, is a multi-level hierarchical structure that serves as the authoritative definition for manufacturing finished goods, sub-assemblies, and the components required to build a product. It is the single source of truth for linking finished Stock Keeping Units (SKUs) to component material procurement.

## Purpose and Definition

The Bill of Materials provides a structured recipe for a finished-good SKU, detailing every component, sub-assembly, and their corresponding quantities needed to build a single finished unit. It explicitly maps finished goods to their raw materials and sub-assemblies, forming a crucial piece of metadata for inventory and supply chain operations.

## Structure and Characteristics

The BOM is structured as a multi-level tree, reflecting the hierarchical nature of product assembly. Key characteristics include:

*   **Hierarchy:** It explicitly defines the parent-child relationships between finished goods, sub-assemblies, and individual components.
*   **Reusability:** A sub-assembly's BOM is defined once and can be referenced globally across different product BOMs, promoting standardization and efficiency.
*   **Versioning:** Revisions to BOM specifications are strictly versioned to ensure that production always operates on a known, approved recipe. Modifications to these specifications are restricted to engineering personnel.

## Role in Inventory and Planning

The BOM is central to inventory management and production planning systems:

*   **SKU Linkage:** It directly links the internal identifier for a distinct product variant (SKU) to the necessary materials. While SKUs are internal identifiers for planning and inventory, BOMs provide the detailed breakdown of what constitutes each SKU. It's important to note that a product can have one UPC/GTIN (an external barcode standard), but multiple SKUs over its lifecycle, and the BOM is defined at the SKU level.
*   **MRP Explosion:** In Material Requirements Planning (MRP), the BOM enables the "explosion" of requirements. When a demand forecast is entered for a finished-good SKU, the planning system uses the BOM to automatically multiply parent demand by the per-unit quantities at every sub-assembly and component level, thereby generating precise procurement purchase demands.

# Inventory Replenishment Parameters Overview

Inventory Replenishment Parameters are critical planning variables that configure order triggers, lead-time variances, and buffer inventory rules across distribution centers (DCs). These parameters, also known as safety stock, reorder point (ROP), and lead time, are fundamental to managing inventory levels effectively and preventing stockouts.

## Key Replenishment Parameters

### Safety Stock

**Safety Stock**, also referred to as **Buffer Stock**, is an inventory cushion held above the demand forecast to absorb variability in demand or late inbound shipments. It is extra inventory maintained to protect against demand spikes and lead-time variability.

*   **Sizing**: Safety stock is typically sized in days of supply or against target service levels, categorized by SKU velocity class:
    *   **Class A (Fast Movers)**: Requires 14 days of supply.
    *   **Class B**: Requires 10 days of supply.
    *   **Class C**: Requires 7 days of supply.

### Reorder Point (ROP)

The **Reorder Point (ROP)** is an inventory trigger, often an ERP-labeled system field, that indicates the on-hand inventory level at which an automatic replenishment order is initiated. Rather than modifying the reorder point directly, planners recalculate the safety stock based on current demand variability, allowing the ROP to adjust automatically.

*   **Formula**: The Reorder Point is calculated using the following formula:
    $ROP = (\text{Average Daily Demand} \times \text{Lead Time in Days}) + \text{Safety Stock}$

### Lead Time

**Lead Time** represents the total elapsed time from when a purchase order (PO) is placed with a supplier until the goods are received, inspected, and posted as available ("good" quantity) to pick. It encompasses supplier processing, transit time, and inbound handling.

*   **Types of Lead Time**:
    *   **Inbound Lead Time**: The time from supplier PO issuance to receipt at a Regional DC.
    *   **Inter-node Lead Time**: The transit time required to move stock from a Regional DC to a Forward DC.

This adjustment automatically recalculates reorder points via standard inventory formulas [Postmortem: Q3 Apparel Class-A Stockouts](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/q3_stockout_postmortem.md).

### Distribution Center (DC) Node Operations
*   **Network Role:** A distribution center (or "fulfillment center/node") acts as an intermediary node in the logistics network, receiving bulk inventory from upstream suppliers and fulfilling downstream orders for retail stores or end customers. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).
*   **Inventory Independence:** Each DC holds, tracks, and counts its inventory independently. Consequently, the same Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) can have highly variable on-hand quantities across different DCs, and replenishment decisions are calculated on a per-DC basis. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

*   **Inbound Quality Control:** Inbound inventory processes require verifying carton counts against the Purchase Order (PO). Good items are posted as available, whereas damaged units are immediately quarantined. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

*   **Persistent Stockouts:** Continuous stockouts of fast-moving SKUs require escalation to **Demand Planning** to re-evaluate safety stock levels and reorder points. Source: [Warehouse Operations Runbook](gs://test-input-gcs-atharva/eval_corpus/warehouse_ops_runbook.md).

# Stock Keeping Unit Tracking Overview

Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) Tracking refers to the management of internal identifiers and their mapping to external barcode standards, which are crucial for running inventory, cycle counts, and logistics routing. This entry describes the core metadata related to product identification and how it underpins inventory management and supply chain operations.

## Key Identifiers and Their Roles

### SKU (Stock Keeping Unit)
The **SKU** is the internal identifier for a distinct, sellable product variant, encompassing specific attributes such as size, color, and pack configuration. It serves as the central hub of the planning stack and represents the fundamental unit at which inventory is held, forecasted, and replenished across all distribution centers. It is important not to confuse a SKU with a UPC/GTIN; a product can have one UPC but multiple SKUs over its lifecycle, and treating them as identical can lead to system double-counting. Putaway and cycle counts must be executed and scanned at the precise SKU level to prevent downstream picking failures. Each distribution center (DC) independently holds, tracks, and counts inventory, meaning SKU quantities can vary across DCs, and replenishment decisions are made per-DC. Real-time on-hand SKU positions directly feed planning system reorder calculations, making accurate cycle counts vital.

### UPC / GTIN (Universal Product Code / Global Trade Item Number)
**UPC / GTIN** refers to an external, industry-wide barcode standard primarily used for retail scanning. In internal systems, it is stored purely as an attribute that is mapped back to an internal SKU.

### Bill of Materials (BOM)
The **Bill of Materials (BOM)** is a multi-level structured recipe that provides the authoritative definition for a finished-good SKU. It lists every component, sub-assembly, and the corresponding quantities required to build a single finished unit. The BOM serves as the single source of truth, linking finished SKUs to component material procurement. Its hierarchy represents a tree structure of finished goods, sub-assemblies, and components. BOMs are defined once for sub-assemblies and referenced globally. Revisions are strictly versioned, ensuring production operates on a known recipe, and only engineering may modify these specifications. When a demand forecast is entered at the finished-good SKU level, the planning system utilizes the BOM to "explode" the requirements, multiplying parent demand by per-unit quantities at every sub-assembly and component level to generate procurement purchase demands.

## Metadata Parameters for Replenishment

SKUs are central to inventory replenishment, which relies on specific metadata parameters:

*   **Safety Stock (Buffer Stock):** This represents extra inventory held to protect against demand spikes and lead-time variability. It is typically sized in days of supply and categorized by SKU velocity class:
    *   Class A (Fast Movers): Standard 14 days of supply, though apparel SKUs were updated to **21 days of supply** due to increased demand variability.
    *   Class B: 10 days of supply.
    *   Class C: 7 days of supply.
*   **Reorder Point (ROP):** This is an ERP-labeled system field that indicates the on-hand inventory level which automatically triggers a replenishment order. The formula for ROP is:
    $ROP = (\text{Average Daily Demand} \times \text{Lead Time in Days}) + \text{Safety Stock}$
*   **Lead Time:** This is the total elapsed time from when a purchase order (PO) is placed with a supplier until the goods are received, inspected, and posted as available ("good" quantity) to pick. It includes supplier processing, transit, and inbound handling.
    *   Inbound Lead Time: Time from supplier PO to receipt at a Regional DC.
    *   Inter-node Lead Time: Transit time required to move stock from a Regional DC to a Forward DC.

## Operational Impact

Inaccurate cycle counts of SKUs negatively affect the timing of replenishment triggers. Persistent stockouts of fast-moving SKUs necessitate escalation to Demand Planning to re-evaluate safety stock levels and reorder points. Discrepancies between physical inbound counts and the Purchase Order for SKUs must be escalated to Procurement.
